messages.author: 5ac683287691482a
messages.subject: Is there a function in Stan analogous to the convolve() function in R?
parts:
Dear User Group,

I am trying to fit a model in Stan that views a particular time-series as arising from the convolution of several “pulses” of varying strength along with a particular response function. As a starting point, I am interested in recreating the analysis reported here by another research tea, (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3365158/) with original scripts in R provided here (http://www.pnas.org/content/suppl/2012/05/11/1201858109.DCSupplemental/sd02.txt and http://www.pnas.org/content/suppl/2012/05/11/1201858109.DCSupplemental/sd03.txt). I have an intuition as to how I should proceed, but a critical step in the original R calculations involves the command:

convolve(i,rev(h),type="open")

Where i represents the pulses and h represents the response function. Does Stan have an equivalent command to convolve(x, y, type='open')? I have been unable to find one.

Cheers!
Jon

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is there a function in Stan analogous to the convolve() function in R?
parts:
I believe that the purpose to which convolve was used in that model was merely to prepare the predictor matrix. You can create that matrix yourself outside Stan, where each column is the response function shifted by a different amount for each column. You then do a standard regression and the weights associated with each column reflect the evidence for a pulse at the time-point corresponding to the shift of that column. 

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~
